candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether weekly declines, rebounds, and repairs were sustained or concentrated, and permit comparison of the observed path with the weekly analyses’ stated horizons. This directly addresses the missing W44 price path and repeated sequence and hindsight concerns.
candidates.evidence_reference: W44 review: no numerical price path; W37–W33 reviews: underlying weekly paths and timestamps absent; daily outputs report only sampled or nominal API horizons with some actual spans shorter than stated.
candidates.metric_name: BTC and ETH hourly price observations with timestamps
candidates.missing_history_problem: Weekly endpoint summaries and irregular multi-hour snapshots cannot establish path ordering or recovery magnitude. Without a continuous historical series, the analyses cannot test whether deterioration preceded drawdowns or whether apparent repairs were substantial.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would make it possible to distinguish persistent participation deterioration or recovery from isolated snapshots, and to compare breadth changes over the same intervals as price and relative-performance changes.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs repeatedly describe Top-100 proxy breadth snapshots with changing membership hashes; W44 review says no breadth series was supplied; W37 and earlier reviews note missing breadth methodology and sequence.
candidates.metric_name: Point-in-time breadth observations with universe membership and calculation metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: Snapshot counts from changing or unspecified universes cannot establish a comparable historical breadth trajectory. The supplied analyses therefore cannot determine whether participation weakness persisted, preceded price weakness, or reversed with rebounds.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would resolve whether the reported single-session or W43 settled-flow observations were part of a persistent flow sequence or an isolated divergence, and permit alignment with price and breadth paths.
candidates.evidence_reference: W44 review: latest supplied settled-flow detail is W43, not W44. Daily outputs repeatedly identify ETF evidence as a single latest settled session, sometimes stale, with intervening sessions unavailable in the supplied context.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF flow rows with settlement dates and reported units
candidates.missing_history_problem: Single-session totals and stale rows cannot establish persistence, within-period sequence, or whether flows diverged between assets during the reviewed weeks. Missing sessions are explicitly not imputed in the analyses.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would preserve which observable warning-related inputs were available at each historical freeze, allowing later path outcomes to be evaluated without relying on completed-week information.
candidates.evidence_reference: W44–W39 reviews cite missing freeze-time warning sequences; W37 and earlier reviews identify absent ex-ante snapshots, issue times, and observation cutoffs. Daily outputs also exclude some forensics snapshots because they post-date the decision cutoff.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped freeze-time observations for the already-reported warning-related inputs
candidates.missing_history_problem: Completed paths and retrospective summaries cannot establish what was observable when an interpretation was formed. Without historical point-in-time snapshots, sequence integrity and hindsight leakage remain untestable.
